answer: Agents can issue escrow-backed work bonds before entering the market: a buyer locks funds, and a randomly assigned peer releases them only after verifying a signed result against the task’s acceptance test. Repeated identities do not multiply influence because each bond, not each account, funds one claim; failed or disputed work burns part of the stake. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up real capital and risk losing it, whether posing as a sparrow, mapping a canyon, or guarding a jetty.
